clue.text: Tied up at work acquiring skill

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tied up with a busy job still manages to pick up a new skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' reads as 'busy at the office', but 'at' is part of the letters to rearrange and 'work' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a natural talent or ability for something is a skill.

clue.text: How's that for charm?

definitions.meaning: in cricket, the fielders' cry asking the umpire to give a batsman out is a formal request of this kind
attractiveness or allure

explanation.surface: Someone fishing for a compliment asks whether their charm worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's that?' (often 'Howzat!') is what cricket fielders shout to ask the umpire to give the batsman out; that shout is called an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's request to the umpire bears the same name as attractiveness or allure, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Contend with an involved situation

definitions.meaning: to fight or quarrel with someone, as in 'don't mess with him'
a confused, complicated muddle

explanation.surface: Advice to grapple with a complicated predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to get into a fight with someone, and a knotted, confused mess of affairs.

clue.text: It's extremely handy for this sort of sketch

definitions.text: It's extremely handy for this sort of sketch

parts.words: It's extremely handy for this sort of sketch
parts.note: the thing at the very end (extremity) of the hand also names a small, quick drawing

explanation.surface: Praise for a tool that is very useful in making a certain kind of drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely handy' means literally at the hand's extremity: the nail on the thumb, which also names a brief sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny rough drawing or brief outline is named after the small nail on a digit.

clue.text: Conclusion is to include North Carolina in the criticism

indicators.note: one word is made to take the other in its middle

parts.note: the final resolution of a plot is its denouement
NC is the US postal abbreviation for North Carolina

explanation.surface: A report's closing section is going to mention a US state as part of its critique.
explanation.walkthrough: A denouement is the final unravelling of a story's plot, hence 'Conclusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a public condemnation or harsh censure is criticism.

clue.text: Just one of them is perfect

definitions.text: Just one of them is perfect

parts.words: Just one of them is perfect
parts.note: in grammar, the perfect is one of the verb forms expressing time, alongside present, past and future

explanation.surface: A grumble that in some group only a single member is flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' is not praise but the grammatical perfect, as in 'I have eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's verb forms marking time include the perfect, so it is one among several such forms.

clue.text: Uplifting holy books are an inspiration to poets

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of holy books
taken as written

explanation.surface: Edifying scriptures inspire those who write verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' reads as 'morally inspiring', but in a down entry it turns OTARE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the Muse of lyric and love poetry, a source of inspiration for poets.

clue.text: Spiders and flies?

definitions.meaning: creatures that make webs from silk
in angling, artificial lures that revolve in the water

explanation.surface: A pairing of predator and prey, spiders and the flies they catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' are not insects here but fishing lures that spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Web-making arachnids and rotating fishing lures are both named for spinning.

clue.text: Is ready and gives support

definitions.meaning: waits prepared to act, as an understudy does
remains loyal to someone, as a friend does

explanation.surface: A description of a dependable helper who is prepared and backs others up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to wait in readiness and to remain loyal to someone.

clue.text: Using new enclosure initially for birds

indicators.note: the pen is placed at the very start of the assembly

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A zoo instruction about putting certain birds into a freshly built enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the enclosure, but it signals rearranging 'Using'; 'initially' says the pen goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Flightless seabirds of the southern hemisphere, so an example of birds.

clue.text: Dad having lost her, I get mum to find her

indicators.note: the word for dad is shown with some letters gone

parts.note: a dad is a father
taken as written, the letters removed
taken as written
MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A family puzzle: with Dad gone, a child turns to Mum to track down a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost her' takes HER from FATHER, leaving FAT. The final 'her' is the definition: the woman named.
explanation.definitionFit: A female name, most famously the Prophet Muhammad's daughter, so a woman referred to as 'her'.

clue.text: Introduce objectives to live within one's income

definitions.meaning: to introduce two parties is to have them meet, and objectives are aims or targets
to manage on the money one earns

explanation.surface: Advice on setting goals for living on what one earns.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: introducing aims to one another is causing goals to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for getting by on one's earnings also reads literally as bringing aims face to face.

clue.text: Actor's instruction to play As You Like It?

definitions.meaning: a stage direction telling a performer to improvise lines

definitions.text: to play As You Like It?
definitions.meaning: to perform however one pleases, from the Latin for 'at pleasure'

explanation.surface: A director telling an actor to perform in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As You Like It' looks like the Shakespeare play, but it is a plain translation of the Latin phrase meaning 'at one's pleasure'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortened Latin for 'at pleasure', used as a direction to improvise freely on stage.

clue.text: Dressed — or nude and natural

indicators.note: to dress something is to arrange it, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A choice between clothes or going naked and natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' looks like the opposite of the answer but is the signal for rearranging OR NUDE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: plain and without decoration, hence natural.

clue.text: Fisherman who does will be more pleased than the boatman

definitions.text: Fisherman who does will be more pleased than the boatman

parts.words: Fisherman who does will be more pleased than the boatman
parts.note: an angler is glad to land a crustacean, while a rower dreads the mishap of the same name

explanation.surface: A comparison of how a fisherman and a boatman feel about a certain outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, the phrase means fouling a stroke by failing to lift the oar out cleanly, a blunder; for an angler it is literal success.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a catch of shellfish, and in rowing a bungled stroke where the oar sticks in the water.

clue.text: A great man in history

parts.note: the Macedonian king who conquered an empire is known by the epithet 'the Great'

explanation.surface: A tribute to a significant historical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great' is not mere praise but the epithet of the Macedonian conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian king who built a vast empire is remembered with the title 'the Great'.

clue.text: Gave credit to writer in the present era

indicators.note: the writer is set inside the era's letters

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the current era of dating
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledged a contemporary author.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to attribute something to someone is to give them credit for it.

clue.text: Anxious when visiting America?

definitions.meaning: agitated and upset
a visitor to the USA is within one of its fifty states

explanation.surface: A traveller feeling nervous about a trip to the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being flustered also reads literally as being inside one of America's states.

clue.text: Wholly dedicated to remaining unmarried?

definitions.meaning: focused on one aim alone
whimsically, someone whose thoughts are set on staying a bachelor or spinster

explanation.surface: Someone utterly committed to never marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined on one purpose, and playfully read as having a mind set on bachelorhood.

clue.text: Stick unusually hard with twice the initial efficiency

indicators.note: the letters appear in an unusual order, so they are rearranged
the chosen letter is used two times over
only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A boast about sticking at something with double the usual efficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice the initial' of efficiency gives EE; 'unusually' then rearranges HARD with EE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cling or be stuck fast to something.

clue.text: Soldiers holding deserter without charge

indicators.note: the soldiers' letters hold the other word inside them

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts a cause, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Troops detain a runaway but bring no formal accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without charge' suggests released with no charge pressed; it means free of cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin-derived word for free, given at no cost.

clue.text: Tiredness affected the inhabitants

indicators.note: affected in the sense of altered, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: Fatigue took its toll on the local population.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people living in a place are its inhabitants.

clue.text: Object is for doctor to take in bird unable to fly

indicators.note: the doctor's letters surround the bird

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A vet complains about being asked to admit a flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to raise an objection or show reluctance is to object.

clue.text: Sliding calculator

definitions.meaning: a creature that slides along: a snake, the viper
a machine or person that adds up figures

explanation.surface: A slide rule, a calculator that works by sliding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sliding calculator' suggests a slide rule, but it is two meanings: a slithering snake and something that sums.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of Britain's venomous viper, which slides along, also means a device that sums numbers.

clue.text: He composed music to support RN vessel

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
a ship of the Royal Navy carries the prefix HMS, His or Her Majesty's Ship

explanation.surface: A musician wrote a piece in support of a Navy ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes, the German Romantic composer of four symphonies and the German Requiem.

clue.text: Whacked a lazy so-and-so

definitions.meaning: informally, utterly exhausted
an idle, shiftless person

explanation.surface: Someone thrashed an idler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whacked' looks like a past-tense verb for hitting, but here it is British slang for worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means exhausted; as one it is a loafer who avoids work or debts.

clue.text: Gloomy feature in arid surroundings

indicators.note: the feature sits inside the other word
the dry word forms the setting around the facial part

parts.note: arid means dry
an ear is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A melancholy characteristic of a desert landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dull, bleak and depressing.

clue.text: Courses for beginners

definitions.meaning: the first dishes of a meal
people or things that start something, such as race entrants

explanation.surface: Classes offered for novices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses for beginners' reads as lessons for novices; it is first dishes and those who begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetisers that open a meal, and people who start a race or game.
